name: RoboBench
description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark covers diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. It introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for planning that assesses embodied feasibility by simulating whether predicted plans can achieve critical object-state changes under physical and visual constraints.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang; Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, Fudan University, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
citeAs: Luo, Y., Fan, C.-K., Dong, M., Shi, J., Zhao, M., Zhang, B.-W., et al. (2025). RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1.
rai:dataCollection: Datasets were built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension data uses daily-life scenarios with explicit instructions rewritten into implicit forms using LLMs. Perception reasoning data is constructed across four aspects: robotic-centric (real robot data with type and view metadata), object-centric (curated static attributes combined with GPT-generated functional properties), scene-centric (Gemini-segmented video steps with manual annotations), and task-centric (human-labeled bounding boxes). Generalized planning data is built from high-quality robotic videos with Gemini-generated structured annotations refined by human annotators. Affordance prediction data is sampled from the planning pool with three types of affordance annotations. Failure analysis data for execution-level failures is collected from RoboMIND and labeled by experts; planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Planning-level failure data lacks real-world examples, so planning failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RDT-1B (Liu et al., 2024b), datasets from Liu et al. (2024c), RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), AgiBot World (Bu et al., 2025), EmbodiedGPT (Mu et al., 2023), data scaling laws dataset (Lin et al., 2024a), and Yang et al. (2024) for navigation; in-house collected robotic data; curated static object attributes from Gao et al. (2024).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit task instructions are rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs. Natural language step descriptions are mapped to predefined function sequences. Function arguments are instantiated with objects extracted from step descriptions. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order). Video frames are extracted as standardized inputs for planning tasks. Affordance annotations include static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile base positions sampled from representative frames.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process is applied: (1) data filtering during construction using general criteria (image quality and task validity) and task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is applied: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail are manually reviewed and corrected. All data are standardized into multiple-choice QA for perception, affordance, and failure dimensions. Planning data uses frame sequences as standardized inputs with structured annotations.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gemini generates structured annotations for planning tasks including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), which are then refined by human annotators. Each step is mapped into function templates. For perception reasoning: robotic-centric uses template-based QA from metadata; object-centric uses GPT-generated functional properties and distractors; scene-centric uses Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding with manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes; task-centric uses human-labeled bounding boxes. Affordance annotations (static, dynamic, navigation) are manually annotated from sampled frames. Execution-level failure annotations are labeled by experts from RoboMIND data. A directed acyclic graph (DAG) capturing inter-step dependencies is human-annotated for planning evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is used for quality control: items that all models solve correctly are removed as too easy, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. Human evaluation of planning data was conducted on 438 uniformly sampled long-horizon tasks, with expert annotators assigning holistic scores (0–20) referencing ground-truth planning lists. Pearson correlation between automated metrics and human scores is reported (r=0.83 for MLLM-as-world-simulator vs r=0.73 for LLM-based baseline), validating the proposed metric.
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition of MLLMs as embodied brains, clarify the role of the embodied brain in robotic systems, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. It aims to advance generalizable embodied intelligence for manipulation in dynamic, unstructured environments.
rai:dataBiases: Planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may bias cross-embodiment planning evaluation. The benchmark relies on large-scale real robotic datasets that may have their own collection biases. Planning-level failure data is synthesized rather than collected from real failures, which may not fully represent real-world failure distributions.
rai:dataLimitations: Planning-level failure data is synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data, which may not capture the full diversity of real failures. The benchmark focuses on manipulation tasks and may not generalize to other embodied AI domains. Execution-level failure diagnosis is intrinsically difficult, with even human evaluators achieving only 47.30 score, indicating the task's inherent complexity. The benchmark covers specific embodiment types (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulator, humanoid) and may not cover all robotic platforms.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and benchmarking of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. Specifically for testing capabilities across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. Provides a leaderboard for comparing state-of-the-art MLLMs and offers actionable insights for advancing embodied brain development in robotic AI.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections. Expert annotators (with prior training) assigned holistic scores for human evaluation of planning data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (Comanici et al., 2025) for generating structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata; GPT for generating functional object properties and distractors; detection models for annotation assistance; LLMs for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit forms.
